doc.citation: Filipiak, P., Zatoń, M., Szaniawski, H., Wrona, R., and Racki, G. 2012. Palynology and microfacies of Lower Devonian mixed carbonate-siliciclastic deposits in Podolia, Ukraine. Acta Palaeontologica Polonica 57(4): 863–877.
doc.comment: The supplied local text contains only the abstract; extraction uses the complete [publisher PDF](https://www.app.pan.pl/archive/published/app57/app20110184.pdf), including visually inspected Table 1 and Fig. 4. DOI metadata verified against [Crossref](https://api.crossref.org/works/10.4202/app.2011.0184). Nine spore-bearing samples and completely weathered IZ−3 are retained. Fig. 4 supplies taxa absent from Table 1. Its caption's 'Emphanisporites var. micrornatus' is treated as the illustrated Table 1 taxon, not an additional occurrence. Quadrisporites is excluded because the authors classify it as an acritarch or alga. Introductory records from Arkhangelskaya (1980), Richardson et al. (1981), Richardson and McGregor (1986), and Turnau in Uchman et al. (2004) are historical context; reuse of their samples is not stated. Spore reworking is not reported; discussed storm reworking concerns skeletal remains. Illustrated flags refer to specimens from the individual sample.

items.depth_or_level: IZ−1; lowermost analysed sample, upper part of the Ivanye Horizon
items.palaeogeo_unit_reported: southwestern margin of the East European Platform
items.age_basis_detail: Emphanisporites micrornatus var. micrornatus identifies the NM Oppel Zone; Amicosporites jonkeri indicates the Si Lineage Zone. Independent conodont dating of the upper Ivanye Horizon by Drygant and Szaniawski (2012) is also cited.
items.setting_as_reported: marginal marine sequences consisting of carbonates intercalated with siliciclastics
items.notes: Palynostratigraphy and palynofacies study also examining marine palynomorphs. Land-derived particles dominate this sample. Quadrisporites sp., illustrated in Fig. 4J, is excluded as algal/acritarch material. Fig. 4L captions the illustrated zonal spore as 'Emphanisporites var. micrornatus'.

items.age_basis_detail: Fig. 3 places Uo−2 in the Lochkovian upper Ivanye Horizon. Its spores have broad Upper Silurian–Lower Devonian ranges and do not permit assignment to a biozone.

items.notes: Poorly preserved, low-diversity land-derived microflora; miospores are rare across the two Ustechko samples and phytoplankton is better represented. Both samples were excluded from quantitative analyses. The broad Upper Silurian–Lower Devonian interval describes spore ranges, rather than a revised depositional age.
